t1.concept: A server answers each request with a status code, headers and a body. The browser reads the Content-Type header to know the body is HTML.
t1.approach: In handle, check the method and the URL first. For GET /, send status 200 with an HTML content type and a small page. Keep the 404 for everything else.
t1.pseudocode:
if the request is GET and the path is "/":
  send status 200 with the type text/html
  send a page whose h1 says Recipe box
  stop
otherwise:
  keep the 404

t3.concept: A host runs your start command on its own machine and gives the app a public URL. Your server must listen on the port the host chooses.
t3.approach: Push the repo to GitHub, then create a free Render web service from it. Use npm start as the start command. The app already reads PORT from the environment.
t3.pseudocode:
push the code
connect the repo on the host
build command: none
start command: npm start
wait for the URL, then open it
